chapter: Small group, new sound and Europe
title: Joe Williams and 'Every Day'
summary: Greene recalls Joe Williams as an usher he'd forgotten and how the hit saved the band.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: 1955, that's a big year.
When you said you think we're going too fast, don't forget there's twenty-two more years to go.
I know. We do have to move now.
1955 you have Joe Williams and Sonny Payne. (laugh)
(laugh) That's right. Oh, yeah.
So, that was 'Every Day.'
That was 'Every Day'.
Did you know Joe Williams before he joined the band?
I don't think so.
Oh. You hadn't seen him in Chicago?
No. I don't think so. I don't remember seeing him. Oh, yes I do, because he was working at the Regal Lincoln Theater.
Yeah. Yeah.
I think he worked there as an usher, or something.
Right.
Am I right?
Something like that.
Something like that.
Yeah. He did something like that.
Yeah, I think he used to -- but, I didn't realize that he was a singer.
Well, when he went with the band, he went with the band like a boy singer, didn't he?

Yes. But, as I say, he made me remember -- and I had forgotten that he had worked at the -- you know -- he used to say -- "You know, I used to be an usher at the --". And, I remember seeing him after, you know, he told me that.
Well, he had sung with Jimmy Noone in another big band in Chicago.
Oh. I didn't know that.
But, when "Every Day" was done, I mean, this has got to be the greatest hit of all.
Yeah. That was it. Actually it was such a hit as far as the public is concerned. I mean, the two together -- Basie and

Joe Williams together, and the band behind it, you know, was such an enormous thing as far as the audience is concerned, and as far as the musicians are concerned -- with the voice -- Joe Williams voice, with the band behind him -- it was a great thing with the two. And, it really left an impression on the public.
Yeah.
Moreso that anybody else that came in there had a hell of a time, you know, as a singer --
Yeah. Trying to follow --
-- trying to follow Joe Williams.
Yeah.

You know, alot of singers have really gone through something. And, he's still going through it, you know, he really left an impression. So, they expect him -- they couldn't realize that -- you know -- they couldn't conceive of the fact that Joe Williams would ever leave the Basie band.
Yeah.
The public enjoyed it so much that they figured that this is going to happen. When it's time to go to see Basie's band you'll look to see Joe Williams.
How long did it last? About two and a half years?
What?
How long did Joe stay with the band?
Oh, longer than that.
Did he?
I think so, yes. I think so. I think he did.
And, then he went out as a single?
Yeah.
And, Basie had a job to try to replace him?
Yes.
Have you still got that fellow that you had at Roseland?
Which one (laugh)?
(laugh) What was his name?
I don't know.
Who was the singer there, rather guy, you know? When you played the dance at Roseland.
The last time? Oh, no, no. Well, I don't know -- he didn't go to Europe with us.
He didn't?
No. So, I --
(laugh) Maybe he'll be back.
I don't know. He might be back after we go back to work -- I don't know. I don't even know his name.
It's Wilson, I think.
Hm? I don't even know his name.
Well, anyway, this Joe Williams thing is really very important, isn't it?
Hm?
I mean, it's very important -- the Joe Williams thing?
Oh, yeah. I mean, with this band. First Jimmy Rushing.
Yeah.

-- Which -- you know -- he did his thing, right? He was it -- you know -- you looked for him. He did a terrific job when he was there. Joe Williams came along -- which is a good -- you know -- second coming in after Jimmy Rushing. And, the people, you know, took to him right away. So, anybody else that come in and don't come up to this -- you know -- how it is.
